Wikipedia's connection row lists SRT Eastern Line, SRT Light Red Line (future) and MRT Orange Line (under construction) - i.e. there is no BTS/MRT interchange at the station today. Nearby exits listed: Pratunam Market, Indra Square, Baiyoke Tower II.

Water: Pratunam pier ~647 m S on Khlong Saen Saep - the line's Golden Mount/NIDA interchange point (operator Family Transport, 100 boats, fares 8-22 THB, 05:30-20:30 weekdays / 19:00 weekends, ~60,000 passengers/day, running since 1990).

claims.text_en: Counter-evidence on transport 9: ARL headway (10-13 min) is roughly 2-5x the BTS Sukhumvit line's (2.40-6.00 min per Wikipedia infobox) and ridership is an order of magnitude apart (70,887/day ARL 2026 Q1 vs 723,167/day BTS 2024). There has been no nonstop Express service from this station at any time (Express suspended September 2014 for rolling-stock shortage; the Makkasan Express was averaging 400 passengers/day), so all airport trips are all-stops City Line. Documented fragility: full suspension 28 Mar 2025 (Myanmar earthquake) and a free-ride week 25-31 Jan 2025 under the PM2.5 policy; the planned 21.8 km extension to Don Mueang had not started construction as of 2024. The dawn-market guide still sends market visitors to BTS Chit Lom/buses/boat rather than the ARL station next door.

claims.text_en: The 3.2 ha park identity and polygon honesty: the only park verifiably both inside the 800 m circle AND inside the computed Voronoi cell is Suan Rom Ratchathewi (สวนรมย์ราชเทวี, OSM way 641160571) - 1.70 ha, 343-471 m NNE along the ARL corridor. Santiphap Park (สวนสันติภาพ, way 99029135): OSM polygon area 2.84 ha but Wikipedia states 8 acres (about 3.2 ha) - matching the app figure; its centroid is 735-824 m NNE, straddling the 800 m edge (nearest vertex 575 m), inside the Ratchaprarop cell but at its margin. Ratchathewi Phirom Park (สวนราชเทวีภิรมย์, 357 Ratchaprarop Rd / Soi Mo Leng; OSM 3.36 ha, 657-833 m ENE) computes to the Makkasan cell. Pathumwananurak (4.45 ha, 663-811 m SSW) computes to the Chit Lom cell. Verdict: the app's '3.2 ha park' is most plausibly Santiphap (Wikipedia 8 acres), which is not fully inside the catchment; alternatively the corridor park cluster (1.70 + 2.84 + 3.36 ha, all edge-adjacent) was summed. Either reading leaves green 8 as the score most exposed to polygon-boundary choice.

Food 8 is anchored by the market food culture: Go-Ang Pratunam Chicken Rice (Hainanese chicken rice since ~1960 on Phetchaburi Rd, Michelin Bib Gourmand - snippet corroboration), Platinum's 6th-floor food court (open to ~21:00 per search snippet), dawn and night market stalls. Nightlife: OSM tags zero nightclubs within 800 m while the app counts 21 venues - the stock is hotel bars, karaoke and rooftops (Baiyoke Sky) rather than clubs (inference; Hotels.com maintains a 'Best Nightlife in Pratunam' roundup).

question_answers.notes: Unit centers exactly on the OSM ARL Ratchaprarop node; City Line-only station (A7, 2010) with no BTS/MRT interchange on site. Verified clips: west = ARL Phaya Thai, east = ARL Makkasan (boundary only ~292 m east of the station), southwest = BTS Ratchathewi; the brief's 'phaya-thai south' guess is wrong. Southern clip (Palladium/pier strip) hinges on whether a BTS Chit Lom unit exists in the app - unresolved.

Two overlapping daily economies: the dawn wholesale garment trade (04:00 setup, 05:00-09:00 trade, cash, 3+ piece minimum, reseller culture) around Baiyoke/Indra Square/Platinum, and the airport-commuter flow through the ARL station (~70.9k daily line ridership). No open source documents porter/logistics specifics for the market belt - recorded as an evidence gap.

Transport 9 = airport line + one-stop BTS transfer + buses + canal-boat pier edge (documented); crowd 3 = documented chaotic market crush; vibe/food 8 = wholesale-market food culture incl. Michelin Bib Go-Ang; nightlife 8 rests on hotel-bar stock OSM does not tag as clubs.

Transport counter: ARL headway 2-5x worse than BTS, ridership 10x smaller, no express since 2014, earthquake suspension Mar 2025, and market guides route around the station. Safety counter: only alleged, tourist-reported incidents (SAYS 2023; 'hell alley' characterization); no unit-level statistics found - the safety-5 pattern remains unverifiable.

Layered hours: stalls from 04:00, dawn wholesale 05:00-09:00 (Mondays thin), Platinum 09:00-20:00, day/retail markets to ~15:00-20:00, evening market ~17:00-21:00 (snippet-corroborated), ARL 05:30-24:00, boats 05:30-20:30.

4 documented street access points on both sides of Ratchaprarop Rd; market-side walking described as crowded/chaotic; no verifiable sidewalk-width or crossing data found. Distances stated, no durations derived: intersection ~517 m, Platinum ~623 m, pier ~647 m.

32 convenience stores within 800 m but no OSM-tagged supermarket inside the circle; groceries via the market belt; Phyathai 1 Hospital ~285 m WNW inside the unit; next general hospitals ~1.0-1.6 km out.

District median asking rent 25,100 THB/mo; 1-BR avg 25,500; near-unit older stock (XT Phayathai, Lumpini Suite Phetchaburi) 18,000-20,500 - matches the 18,000/38,000 district blend and supports rent 7 as moderate. Asking prices and district-level aggregation are the caveats.

Only 1.70 ha (Suan Rom Ratchathewi) is verifiably inside both circle and Voronoi cell. The 3.2 ha figure most plausibly = Santiphap Park (Wikipedia 8 acres; OSM 2.84 ha), whose centroid straddles the 800 m edge. The other 3+ ha parks compute to neighboring units. Green 8 is the score most exposed to boundary choice; 'quiet' is undercut by dawn-market logistics and arterial traffic.
Strong fit for airport commuters, garment traders/resellers and budget shoppers; poor fit for high-frequency-rail households, quiet/green-seeking residents, and big-box grocery shoppers.

Biggest structural change: MRT Orange Line west section construction started 31 Jul 2024 and will put an MRT interchange under Ratchaprarop Rd (opening target July 2030), ending the 'ARL-only' condition this control entity tests. ARL contactless from 8 Nov 2025; earthquake suspension 28 Mar 2025. Market livestream-reseller conflict ongoing since ~2022. No verified market redevelopment decision.

Transport-9 mechanism is documented (airport line + Phaya Thai BTS one stop + buses + pier) but rests on an all-stops line with 10-13 min headways - not an interchange premium; safety-5 has zero unit-level statistics; park identity is a boundary artifact; gym_sports 9 is the least-evidenced score (OSM: Anytime Fitness, Topkart, 2 pools within 1200 m - hotel gyms likely drive it, inference).

preview.text_en: The airport-rail control unit: ARL Ratchaprarop, Pratunam's garment economy at the door, a 1.7 ha pocket park — and an MRT Orange Line interchange arriving ~2030.

guide_lead.text_en: Ratchaprarop is the app's ARL-only control: no BTS or MRT interchange, just City Line service (10-13 min headways) to Suvarnabhumi and a one-stop transfer at Phaya Thai. Its transport 9 is 'airport rail plus everything nearby' — Pratunam's wholesale blocks, Platinum Fashion Mall's economy and the Pratunam canal pier — not rail density. Suan Rom Ratchathewi (1.70 ha, 343-471 m) is the verifiable in-unit green; the mapped 3.2 ha figure matches Santiphap Park straddling the 800 m edge. Safety 5 repeats the dataset's unanchored pattern. The MRT Orange Line runs under Ratchaprarop Road with an ARL interchange targeted for July 2030.

strengths.text_en: Airport rail at the door: ARL City Line headways of 10-13 minutes and 70,887 daily riders (2026 Q1) make airport commuting the unit's defining convenience.
Suan Rom Ratchathewi (1.70 ha, 343-471 m) is polygon-verified in-unit green.

tradeoffs.text_en: Transport 9 has no interchange behind it: ARL headways trail BTS 2.4-6 minutes, and the unit depends on buses and walking for non-airport trips.
Safety 5 is the third entity in a row with zero unit-level statistics; only alleged tourist-scam reports (bag-slicing, pickpocket alleys) exist.

day_night.text_en: Wholesale-market hours set the day; the garment district's evenings thin earlier than the nearby hotel belt.

within_area_variation.text_en: The ARL/Pratunam frontage differs from the quieter Ratchaprarop sois west toward Santiphap.

conditional_fit.text_en: Strong fit: airport commuters and wholesale-market traders; the control condition expires when the Orange Line interchange opens (~July 2030).

uncertainties: rating transport (9): Defensible only as 'airport rail + everything nearby', not as interchange quality: no BTS/MRT interchange on site today, headway 10-13 min vs BTS 2.4-6 min, express never served this station. The MRT Orange Line interchange under construction (opening target 2030) will retroactively validate the 9, but the rating describes a pre-2030 condition.

rating rent (7): District blend (18,000/38,000 editorial) is corroborated by FazWaz (median 25,100; 1-BR avg 25,500; older Baiyoke-side stock 18,000-20,500). Own-stock evidence puts the unit's older condos at the affordable end of the district band - rent 7 holds as 'moderate'.

rating daily_essentials (9): Convenience density (32 stores, 25+ 7-Eleven) plus the market belt plus Phyathai 1 Hospital at ~285 m. Note the OSM absence of any supermarket inside 800 m - the 9 leans on small-format retail, which matches how the district actually shops.

rating safety (5): Third entity in a row where safety 5 has no unit-specific statistical support. Evidence is reported-perception only (alleged bag-slicing 2023; 'hell alley' pickpocket-prone alley; citywide #1 pickpocket ranking). The score should be understood as a placeholder for an unverifiable mid-band, not a measurement.

rating food (8): Market food culture is well documented (Go-Ang Bib Gourmand; Platinum food court; dawn/night stalls); 336 app food venues vs 94 OSM-tagged eateries shows OSM under-coverage, not app inflation.

rating green (8): Weakest-supported high score: only 1.70 ha verifiably in-unit; the 3.2 ha figure most plausibly names Santiphap Park, whose centroid straddles the 800 m edge and whose Voronoi ownership is boundary-dependent. Flag for polygon review.

rating gym_sports (9): Least-evidenced score in open data: OSM shows Anytime Fitness, Topkart, 2 pools (1200 m radius) and 8 pitches. The 9 plausibly counts hotel gyms/pools (Baiyoke, Novotel Platinum) - researcher inference, no direct source. Flag.

rating vibe (8): Trade-market character with a skyline anchor (304 m Baiyoke II at ~200 m) and a documented 'colorful and chaotic' tourist framing; vibe 8 reads as day-market energy, not evening leisure.
rating nightlife (8): 21 venues vs 0 OSM nightclubs: the stock is hotel bars/karaoke/rooftops. The score is plausible but its composition (late-closing hotels vs dedicated nightlife) is unverified.

rating crowd (3): Best-corroborated negative: every source describes crush conditions (dawn market hell-alley, 'armies of local vendors', chaotic streets). Crowd 3 is honest and possibly conservative for mid-day market hours.
